measurements.visual_note: The right column's four sections of one-line items leave loose, floating white space (Cider stands alone between two 36 pt gaps), while the left column is dense with two-line cocktail entries. The page is balanced in metrics but not by eye.

top_problem: The design has no ownable idea. A papel picado banner, agave sprigs and bilingual kickers are the stock Mexican-cantina kit seen on a thousand menus, laid over a tidy two-column list. On my lens, the House Originals panel breaks the one column rule it depends on: names and prices shift 3.5 mm off the column's edges. The boldest missing idea is a real graphic system taken from Mexican cut-paper and loteria culture, such as each section as a numbered loteria card or the papel picado cut pattern used as the grid itself, rather than trim at the top.
fixes: Keep the House Originals names, descriptions and prices on the column's 36 pt left edge and 294 pt right edge, and push the panel frame and tint outward by 10 pt into the gutter and margin, so column 1 has one left edge and one price edge (currently 3.53 mm spread on both).

Move House Originals to the prime top-left position above Classics and give it a stronger treatment, such as a larger name size or a signature illustration, because the high-margin originals now sit mid-column below commodity classics.

Replace the generic banner-and-sprig trim with one ownable system tied to the venue, such as loteria-card section frames with numbers, a cut-paper pattern built on the 12 pt grid, or a custom wordmark instead of the generic 'Cantina & Cocktail Bar' set in Fraunces.

Rebalance the right column so it fills by eye as well as by numbers: set Cider as a subheader under Beer, or add glass/bottle price columns for wine, so there are no floating one-item islands and 36 pt holes.

Give the thin one-line descriptions (e.g. 'Hop-forward IPA.', 'Dry red wine.') proper grape, region, style and ABV lines, so the item rhythm matches the two-line cocktails and the texture across both columns reads as one design.

top_problem: The hierarchy is clean but broken in three measurable places. (1) The right column's headers are one 24 pt row off from the left column's. Wine sits at y 177.01 mm and Spirits at 185.47 (8.46 mm). BY THE GLASS sits at 190.50 and AGAVE at 198.97. SPARKLING sits at 228.60 and BRANDY at 237.07. Only Cocktails and Beer share a line (75.41 mm), so the headers stagger across the gutter. (2) The top-level Cider header, 24 pt with its Sidra kicker, carries a single item and is the only section with no subheader. That is two patterns for the same level, and it leaves large holes in the right column (about 16 mm above Cider and about 16 mm above Wine, against about 9 mm above Spirits). proposal.md line 230 says Cider was folded into Beer and Wine was levelled with Spirits, but the render does neither. (3) The House Originals panel indents its subheader and item names to 46 pt against 36 pt, and its prices end at 284 pt against 294 pt. This fails the section 4 measured checks for subheader x, item-name x and price right edge (1 column spread 3.53 mm), so criteria 1, 2 and 3 are capped at 40. On concept, this is a tidy two-column list with papel picado trim. The missing big idea is a Lotería-card system: each section becomes a numbered Lotería card ("No. 1 La Margarita", "El Agave") with its own cut-paper illustration and a card-frame header. That would make the headers themselves the narrative rather than a bold word plus an italic Spanish echo.
fixes: Make Cider a CIDER subheader under Beer (styled like DRAFT), as the proposal already claims, then re-flow the right column so Wine, By the Glass and Sparkling share y with Spirits, Agave and Brandy (185.47 / 198.97 / 237.07 mm) and the gutter reads as one set of rows.

Stop indenting inside the House Originals panel: keep the subheader and item names at x 36 pt and prices at a right edge of 294 pt, and mark the panel with a full-column tint plus a terracotta rule or the corner ticks outside the text, so every column-1 subheader, name and price shares one edge.

Make the space above a section header visibly larger than the space above a subheader (for example 48 pt against 24 pt) and identical everywhere, including after the framed panel, so the two levels are told apart by spacing as well as by size.

Give section headers a stronger mark than a 24 pt word plus an italic kicker, such as a numbered cut-paper card or tile frame, a marigold numeral, or a hairline that locks the kicker to the header, so the hierarchy is ownable rather than generic.

Fill or rebalance the empty bands under Amber Lager, Dry Cider and Pinot Grigio (for example move Brandy or House Originals content) so both columns carry equal density rather than ending level only because of padding.

lens: palette, contrast, price and number styling
top_problem: The page is a tidy two-column list with papel-picado trim: clean, but you have seen it at every cantina. The terracotta/agave/marigold palette is correct but predictable, and the prices are small terracotta serifs that never become a designed element. The boldest missing idea is a real system rooted in the venue, such as the proposal's own Lotería card concept: numbered cards with their own icons, where the price and card number become the graphic signature. Measurements: every text colour passes contrast (ink 14.69, #A63C1A 5.55 on #F6EEDF and 5.05 on the #F1E4CF panel, agave 6.50, adobe 7.33). Marigold #E3A018 is 1.96:1, but it is only used for ornaments. Col 1 price right edges are 284 and 294 pt (3.53 mm spread, because the panel insets them), so one column has two price edges. col2 is 0.00 mm. Margins are 36 pt on all sides. The documents disagree about prices: proposal.md says Fraunces 600 at 13 pt, layout.json says 500 at 12 pt. The changelog also says Cider was folded into Beer and the flags now use one terracotta, but the preview still shows a stand-alone Cider/Sidra section and layout.json keeps #B4441F for the flags. Two terracottas that almost match read as a mistake, not intent.
fixes: Build the Lotería concept: turn each section into a numbered card with a bespoke cut-paper icon, and make the card number and prices one styled numeral system (for example, oversized Fraunces numbers in an agave-green or terracotta tab) so the numbers become the menu's signature.

Put all col-1 prices on one right edge (294 pt): either let the House Originals prices hang out to the column edge past the panel padding, or drop the framed panel in favour of a full-width tint band, so a section never has two price columns.

Use a single terracotta (make the flags #A63C1A too, or deliberately separate the two roles), and give marigold a stronger job, such as the panel ground or a price-tab fill with ink numerals, so the palette looks authored and not just correct.

Reconcile the documents with the render: set one price spec (weight and size) in proposal.md and layout.json, and either fold Cider into Beer as the changelog says or correct the changelog, because the Cider section and its big whitespace gap throw off the right column's rhythm.

Give the price numerals more presence without shouting (for example tabular old-style figures at the item-name size, or a thin leader or dot to the name) so the price reads as part of each line and not as a stray red number at the far edge.

top_problem: This is a tidy two-column list with stock papel picado and agave trim. Any Mexican restaurant in the country could use it, and nothing in it belongs to this cantina or to Iowa City. The boldest missing idea is an ownable system: for example a lotería-card concept where each section is a numbered card (El Coctel, La Cerveza, El Agave...) with its own illustrated plate, or a cut-paper system where the papel picado runs through the whole structure (section frames, dividers, price marks) instead of being a header banner. On top of that, the inset House Originals panel breaks the left column's name and price edges by 3.53 mm, which is a measured failure on criteria 1 and 3.
fixes: Make the House Originals panel a full-column-width tint (item names at x=36pt, prices right-aligned to 294pt), with the frame and corner ticks drawn outside the text measure, so the left column's name and price edges measure 0.0 mm spread and criteria 1 and 3 are uncapped.

Build one ownable concept (lotería-style numbered section cards, or papel picado cut-paper frames and dividers used throughout) so the culture drives the structure instead of decorating the top and bottom.

Move House Originals to the prime top-left position above Classics, and give it a larger signature treatment (a bigger name size or a small illustration per drink), because it holds the high-margin drinks.
Replace the generic 'Cantina & Cocktail Bar' masthead with a real wordmark treatment (custom lettering, a cut-paper ligature or a stamped seal) so the menu reads as one venue, not a category.
Even out the right column visually: tighten the ink gap between Amber Lager and Cider, and hang a small agave or flag ornament at the Wine end, so both columns end level in ink, not just in slots.

top_problem: The phone is the print page stacked into one column. It has no mobile idea of its own. It inherits the print column order (Cocktails, then Spirits, then Beer, a one-item Cider section, then Wine), so a scrolling guest has to hunt for beer and wine below the neat pours. The papel picado sits only in the masthead and never returns as a system. The biggest missing idea is to make the cut-paper flag the menu's structure: each section opens under its own pierced flag in its own colour (terracotta for agave and cocktails, marigold for beer, green for wine), with section motifs punched from the flag lace. On the phone that becomes a sticky flag tab bar, so both formats read as one festival banner instead of a clean list with festive trim.

Carry the papel picado past the masthead: give each section header a small pierced-flag tab in a consistent assigned colour, and on the phone make those tabs a sticky jump bar, so the concept runs the whole length of a 5,600 px scroll.

Make the phone banner symmetric (for example 5 flags ordered red, yellow, green, yellow, red, or an odd repeat centred on the green agave flag) and use one terracotta for flags and prices, as the proposal states.

Give the thin one-line spirits, beer and wine entries a visual rhythm on the phone, such as a compact two-column name/price list or a denser item gap, so the lower half does not read as one long, evenly spaced, empty list after the rich cocktail panel.

Pull the phone title onto one tracked line or set an intentional stacked lockup, with the ampersand on its own line or the words centred on the ampersand, instead of the default wrap after 'Cantina &'.

lens: every item and price vs the draft (build/draft_doc.json)
top_problem: All 14 draft items are present, nothing is invented, and all 14 prices match the draft exactly. The menu still fails the content bar because only the 4 cocktails have real descriptions. The other 10 items print placeholder text straight from the draft: wine has no grape detail or region ('Dry red wine.'), beer and cider have no ABV, and the spirit lines just repeat the item name ('Blanco tequila pour.', 'VSOP Cognac pour.'). The missing_ingredients flags for these gaps exist only in doc.json, so a guest or the venue sees stub copy. The categories are not treated equally. Separately, the inset House Originals box moves the 16 and 14 prices 10 pt (3.53 mm) left of the other column-1 prices, which sit at 294 pt. That breaks the rule that prices share one column within the Cocktails section. The cocktail garnish and serve text (lime wheel, on the rocks, coupe, orange peel, large cube, lime coin) is not in the draft components, so content could not trace it; the accuracy reviewer should confirm it against phg.recipe_versions. One draft line was edited without a note: 'Hop-forward draft IPA.' became 'Hop-forward IPA.'
fixes: Get the missing facts flagged in missing_ingredients from the venue and print them: wine grape and region (Malbec, Pinot Grigio, Brut Rosé), beer and cider style plus ABV, and spirit brand plus age or pour. Until then, show a visible 'details to come' marker instead of stub copy, and replace the name-repeating spirit lines ('Blanco tequila pour.') with type/age wording from known facts only.

Right-align the House Originals prices to the column-1 price edge at 294 pt, either by running the box's inner padding to the column edge or by moving the prices outside the box, so all Cocktails prices share one right edge (±0.3 mm).
Restore the draft wording 'Hop-forward draft IPA.', or record the edit in designer_notes; content changes need a note.
Record a source for each added garnish and serve fact in designer_notes (the phg.recipe_versions garnish, glassware and method row); if a fact has no source, remove it from the description.

Bring the non-cocktail copy up to the cocktail standard using facts the venue confirms. This fixes the tone split (rich cocktail copy vs one-line stubs) and the unequal treatment of drinks categories, which hold criteria 5 and 10 down.

top_problem: Only the 4 cocktails have complete ingredient descriptions. The other 10 of 14 items (3 spirits, 3 beers, cider, 3 wines) still print the draft's one-line placeholders. 'Blanco tequila pour.', 'Añejo tequila pour.' and 'VSOP Cognac pour.' just repeat the item name. The beers have a style but no ABV, and the wines have a grape but no region. All of it is honestly flagged in meta.missing_ingredients, but the page reads as half a menu.
fixes: Close the flagged gaps with a source-data lookup (tequila and cognac brand and age, beer ABV and brewery, wine region and producer, cider ABV), or with answers from the venue. Rewrite the 10 thin lines from the results so each one says more than the item name. This is the biggest lift, for criteria 8 and 10.

Until that data arrives, get the venue to answer the questions already open in doc.meta: Brut Rosé glass or bottle, pour sizes, the Manhattan's aromatic bitters (the draft line says them but the printed line drops them), and the retired Junmai Ginjo. Then print pour and serve labels (for example '2 oz' or 'glass') in one consistent style next to the prices.
Put the draft's 'Bright and citrus-forward' back on the Margarita by tightening the serve line (for example drop 'served'), so the finished copy does not lose a tasting note the draft already had.
Pull the House Originals prices out to the column's shared right edge at 294 pt (they now end 3.53 mm inside it, at 284 pt), so all 7 left-column prices share one right edge.

Check the drinks order against the scorecard's suggested flow (cocktails, beer, wine, spirits, non-alcoholic), which puts spirits after wine; right now the order by column is Cocktails, Spirits, Beer, Cider, Wine. Also, one Dry Cider under its own 5th section header takes up a lot of space and pushes Wine down. Either keep the section and add a proposal note on why, or ask the venue whether Cider can sit under Beer as a subheader, as the draft's sec_cider structure permits.
problems: Criterion 9: all 14 prices exactly match build/draft_doc.json, and nothing is invented, changed or dropped; items_rendered is 14 and printed_prices_match_doc is true. The retired Junmai Ginjo is left off, and this is noted. There are no $ signs and no glass/bottle labelling.

Criterion 8: the cocktails are complete (spirit, modifiers, garnish, method and serve, all traced to draft components). The spirits lines give no age or type beyond the name. The beers lack ABV, the wines lack region, and the cider lacks ABV. All of this is flagged, not invented, so it is not an automatic fail, but description completeness is weak.

Criterion 8: the Manhattan prints without the 'aromatic bitters' that its draft line has, because public_components has them hidden. This is flagged as a question, but for now the printed recipe is less complete than the draft.
Criterion 10: the tone splits. The cocktail copy is two lines of guest language; everything else is one-line, database-flat text. Visually it reads as one design, but the copy does not.

Criterion 5: House Originals is well featured in its terracotta frame. The column-bottom measure reports [720, 720] pt, but by the proposal's own admission the right column's content ends at 696 pt, and in the preview it is visibly shorter than the left. No non-alcoholic section exists; the draft has none either, and the proposal flags this as a risk.

lens: flow and section order for a Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar in Iowa City
top_problem: The flow does not sell the cantina. The framed prime spot, the best position on the page, goes to a Brown Butter Old Fashioned and a Daiquiri, while the Margarita (the likely best seller and the venue's signature) sits unframed in Classics next to a Manhattan. The right column also ends 24 pt short of the left, with loose air around a one-item Cider section that gets a full H1. The page reads like a generic bar list with Spanish labels, not a Mexican cocktail bar. Prices match the draft exactly: all 14 items, no changes, nothing added or dropped. The order changed from the draft's Cocktails > Beer > Wine > Spirits > Cider to Cocktails > Spirits | Beer > Cider > Wine. Putting agave next to cocktails is defensible for this venue, but proposal.md never explains the reorder. Beer shows no ABV, wine shows no region, and spirits show no brand; these are flagged in meta.missing_ingredients but not resolved. Several lines only repeat the item name ('Blanco tequila pour.', 'VSOP Cognac pour.', 'Dry red wine.'). The col-1 price right edge spreads 3.53 mm because the framed box is inset 10 pt.
fixes: Give the prime framed slot to agave: make the Margarita the lead, or frame the whole Cocktails block with it on top, and keep the Old Fashioned and Daiquiri below as house originals, so the first thing the eye lands on is the drink that defines a cantina.

Fold the one-item Cider into Beer as a 'Cider' subheader under 'Beer & Cider' (or state in proposal.md why the draft's separate sec_cider must stay a full H1), and use the freed space to level the right column with the left at 720 pt.
Justify the change from the draft's section order in proposal.md, and confirm with the Coordinator that the Cocktails > Spirits (agave first) | Beer > Cider > Wine order is approved for this venue.

Get ABV and origin for the three beers, region for the Malbec, Pinot Grigio and Brut Rosé, and brand/age for both tequilas and the Cognac through needs_input, then replace the name-repeating lines ('Blanco tequila pour.', 'Añejo tequila pour.', 'VSOP Cognac pour.', 'Dry red wine.') with fact-based copy.
Align the framed House Originals prices to the col-1 price edge at 284 pt (or document one deliberate inset edge for the box) so the left column has one price right edge.
problems: No Non-Alcoholic section: none in the draft either, so do not invent one, but flag it as an open question for a college-town audience.
Right column bottom is 696 pt against 720 pt on the left, leaving visible dead space around Cider and between Beer and Wine.

top_problem: The menu reads in two voices. The four cocktails get full copy (spirit, modifiers, garnish, method and serve), but the ten beer, wine, spirit and cider items keep draft stubs. Some of those stubs repeat the item name: 'Blanco Tequila' is described as 'Blanco tequila pour.', 'Añejo Tequila' as 'Añejo tequila pour.', 'Cognac VSOP' as 'VSOP Cognac pour.' and 'Dry-Hopped IPA' as 'Hop-forward IPA.' Others use category wording, such as 'Dry red wine.' and 'Dry white wine.' Across the whole right column, no ABV, grape region, producer or age is printed, so half the page looks unfinished. Separately, proposal.md contradicts itself and the render. Line 230 says Cider was folded into Beer, the 'Sidra' kicker was removed and there are no cactus, heart or moon icons. Line 105 lists cactus, corazón and moon flags. doc.meta.designer_notes and the preview both show Cider as its own section with a 'Sidra' kicker. Prices all match: all 14 items are in both the draft and the proposal, with no changed, dropped or invented prices, and the retired Junmai Ginjo is correctly left off and noted.
fixes: Bring the non-cocktail copy up to the cocktail voice using only known facts. Where a stub repeats the item name (the three spirit pours and 'Hop-forward IPA.'), say how it is served instead, for example 'Neat or on the rocks', if the recipe or serve data supports that. Otherwise print a short placeholder line and leave the fields in meta.missing_ingredients, rather than printing a stub that just repeats the name.

Get the venue's answers to the open items in meta.missing_ingredients before print: beer ABV and style, wine region and producer, and the tequila and Cognac brand. Criterion 8 cannot pass 80 while every beer, wine and spirit item lacks its required facts (beer ABV, wine region, spirit brand/age).

Rewrite proposal.md so it matches the actual render and doc.json. Choose one Cider treatment (a standalone section, or folded under Beer) and one flag-motif list, delete the contradicting passage, and make the render match whichever you choose.

Fix the section flow. A one-item Cider section with its own full-size header gets as much space as Wine. Fold it into Beer as a 'CIDER / Sidra' subheader. Also consider a reading order of Cocktails, then Spirits (agave), then Beer and Cider, then Wine, and explain the choice for an agave-led cantina in the proposal.

Raise the Manhattan's hidden bitters with the venue as a blocking question. A Manhattan printed with only rye and sweet vermouth reads as incomplete to a trade reader, even though hiding them correctly follows the public_components flag.

lens: how missing data is handled and flagged
top_problem: Missing data is flagged in doc.json but never shows up in the design. 10 of the 14 items (all spirits, beer, cider and wine) print thin placeholder lines such as 'Blanco tequila pour.', 'Dry red wine.' and 'Dry sparkling rosé.'. These restate the item name and leave out the facts the scorecard requires: grape and region, ABV, age or brand. The flags themselves have gaps and use inconsistent key names. Brut Rosé has no 'grape' flag even though its grape is unknown. The same fact is keyed as brand, brewery and producer on different items. Non-ingredient facts (vintage, glass_or_bottle) are filed under missing_ingredients. The round-4 proposal has no ranked 'blocking before print' list and no risk_flags block. It also no longer flags that the draft has no non-alcoholic section. Cross-checks against build/draft_doc.json: all 14 items and prices match exactly, with nothing invented or dropped. The retired Junmai Ginjo is left off and noted. The Manhattan's hidden bitters are noted with the public_components source. Other findings: 'Bright and citrus-forward' was cut from the Margarita to fit the layout, not for a content reason. Inside the House Originals frame, prices sit 10 pt (3.53 mm) left of the Classics prices in the same Cocktails section. The Brut Rosé sits under 'Sparkling', not 'By the Glass', and its price has no glass/bottle label. The proposal contradicts itself on column bottoms: it says [720, 720] and also says the right column ends at 696. The render shows large empty gaps below Beer and Cider.
fixes: Replace doc meta.missing_ingredients with one normalised meta.missing_facts list per item using a fixed key set (producer, grape, region, vintage, abv, pour_size, age_statement, serve_size_label), add 'grape' to Brut Rosé, and put one ranked 'Needs input before print' table in proposal.md that marks which gaps block printing (wine region and grape, beer ABV, pour sizes, Brut Rosé glass or bottle).

Until the venue supplies the data, write the category lines only from facts already known, never repeating the item name (for example Añejo Tequila: 'Aged tequila, served neat'; Malbec: 'Malbec, red'; IPA: 'India pale ale, dry-hopped'), and leave space for the flagged ABV, region and pour size so the layout will not reflow when they arrive.
Add a glass or bottle label to the Brut Rosé price (it is flagged glass_or_bottle), or confirm it is by the glass, so every wine price shows its serve.

Put the House Originals prices on the same right edge as the Classics prices (294 pt) by letting the frame extend outward instead of insetting its contents, so the Cocktails section has a single price column.

Restore the draft's 'Bright and citrus-forward' on the Margarita (or get the venue's sign-off to cut it) instead of trimming copy to fit, fix the 720-vs-696 contradiction in proposal.md, and flag the missing non-alcoholic section as an open question.

lens: trace printed ingredients, garnishes, glass and serve to gateway rows (gateway log_id 106: phg.menu_items joined to phg.recipe_versions on current_recipe_version_id, project ddc4bb5b)
top_problem: Every cocktail fact traces to a source row, and nothing is invented. I checked all four: Margarita rv f06abb74 (Lime wheel, Rocks, strained over fresh ice), Manhattan rv 9fb77eaa (Cocktail cherry, Coupe, stirred and strained), Brown Butter Old Fashioned rv 7095fd3d (Orange peel, Rocks, over a large cube) and House Daiquiri rv 14d45e57 (Lime coin, Coupe, fine strain, plus the 'House 1:1 demerara' note). The copy itself is the problem. Criterion 12 falls into the automatic-fail band because the three spirits lines only repeat their item names ('Blanco tequila pour.', 'Añejo tequila pour.', 'VSOP Cognac pour.'). The wine, beer and cider lines read like database categories ('Dry red wine.', 'Dry white wine.', 'Hop-forward IPA.'). On top of that, proposal.md describes a menu that is not the one rendered. It says Cider was folded into Beer as a subheader, that the 'Sidra' kicker was removed, that the Margarita reads 'over fresh ice' and that the Old Fashioned prints 'aromatic bitters'. The PNG shows a separate Cider section with a Sidra kicker, 'Shaken, served on the rocks.' and plain 'bitters'.
fixes: Rewrite the spirits and still-wine lines in guest language using only sourced facts, or leave them blank and flag missing_ingredients (producer, age, pour size, grape origin), so no description just repeats its item name.

Bring proposal.md into line with round-4/preview-letter.png and doc.json: Cider is a separate section with a Sidra kicker, the Margarita reads 'served on the rocks', the Old Fashioned reads 'bitters'. Delete the stale round-3 wording, which makes coherence and traceability impossible to audit.

Restore the draft wording 'Hop-forward draft IPA.' (menu_items Dry-Hopped IPA). Either print the Manhattan's Aromatic Bitters, which are in both rv 9fb77eaa and the draft description, or cite the public_components row that hides them.
Give Brut Rosé (13) a glass or bottle label and put pour-size labels on the spirits. Right now 'Sparkling' sits outside 'By the Glass' with no format, so a guest cannot tell what 13 buys.

Layout note for the designer: the description measure splits the garnish and serve phrases across lines ('lime / wheel', 'served / up in a coupe'). Tighten the measure or hold each phrase together with a non-breaking space. The House Originals prices sit 3.53 mm inside the column's price edge (measured_checks col1 price_right_spread_mm), so align them with the column.

lens: description quality and one guest voice
top_problem: The menu is written in two voices. The four cocktails get full recipe-card lines, and every one checks out against phg.recipe_versions: Margarita is Rocks / Lime wheel / 'Shake with ice and strain over fresh ice'; Manhattan is Coupe / Cocktail cherry / 'Stir with ice and strain'; Brown Butter Old Fashioned is Rocks / Orange peel / 'Stir with ice and strain over a large cube'; House Daiquiri is Coupe / Lime coin, with 'house demerara syrup' taken from its phg.menu_items.menu_description. But the 11 spirits, beer, cider and wine lines are the phg.menu_items.menu_description text printed word for word, and several of them just repeat the item name in trade words: 'Blanco tequila pour.', 'Añejo tequila pour.', 'VSOP Cognac pour.', 'Hop-forward IPA.', 'Dry sparkling rosé.' (under Brut Rosé). 'Dry red wine.' and 'Dry white wine.' say nothing a guest would want. That is the automatic fail for criterion 12 (name repeated, database wording). proposal.md line 101 says the taxonomy words are gone and the wine lines no longer repeat the name, but preview-letter.png and doc.json show the draft text unchanged, so the proposal notes do not match what was rendered. Even the cocktail lines read like a prep sheet ('Shaken, served on the rocks.'). The only appetising words the draft had, 'Bright and citrus-forward' (Margarita menu_description), were cut to save a line.
fixes: Rewrite every non-cocktail line from sourced facts only so none of them repeats the item name or uses 'pour'. lens: venue-type fit (Mexican cantina and cocktail bar, Spanish usage, census ZCTA 52240)
top_problem: Round 4 has no invented facts, but it doesn't read like a cantina. Three spirit lines just restate the item name, which is an automatic fail on criterion 12: 'Blanco Tequila / Blanco tequila pour.', 'Añejo Tequila / Añejo tequila pour.' and 'Cognac VSOP / VSOP Cognac pour.'. 'Dry Cider / Dry sparkling cider.' and 'Dry-Hopped IPA / Hop-forward IPA.' come close. The agave list is two generic pours placed below the cocktails, and the header is the generic 'Cantina & Cocktail Bar'. For ZCTA 52240 (phg_census_zcta: median age 28.6, 29.9% aged 21-34, 47.6% with a bachelor's degree or higher, 11% Hispanic/Latino, median household income $52,960) the menu should lead with agave and Mexican serves. Instead its emphasis on Czech Pilsner, Cognac and Pinot Grigio could belong to any Midwest bar.
fixes: Replace the three spirit stubs that repeat the item name with guest-language lines built only from sourced facts. Use the spirit_lexicon or beverage_categories rows for blanco, añejo and VSOP (for example, what the añejo age class means), and flag brand and pour_size as missing, as meta.missing_ingredients already does, rather than printing 'pour'.

Give tequila its conventional cantina order and match the draft component's spelling by printing 'Tequila Blanco' / 'Tequila Añejo'. The Margarita component in recipe f06abb74 reads 'Tequila Blanco', but its printed line says 'Blanco tequila'. Changing the item names themselves is the designer's decision, so send it as a note.

Use one voice everywhere. The cocktails read as a technical spec ('Shaken, served on the rocks.', 'Stirred, served up in a coupe.'), and every other item gets a two-to-three-word stub. Either work each cocktail's serve into an appetising phrase or give the beer, cider and wine the same depth, with no new facts: request ABV, brewery, region and producer through missing_ingredients.

Label pours and prices: the Sparkling subhead leaves the Brut Rosé 13 ambiguous (glass or bottle; glass_or_bottle is still missing), and beers and spirits print no pour size. Add a 'copa / botella' or 'pint' label next to the prices once the data exists. Also send a layout note: the prices inside the House Originals box end at 284 pt while the rest of column 1 ends at 294 pt (measured_checks col1 price_right_spread 3.53 mm), which breaks the price edge.

Carry the Spanish pairing through consistently. Agave and Brandy are the only subheads with no italic pair. Keep the correct usages (Cócteles, Destilados, Cerveza, Sidra, Vino, Clásicos, De la casa, De barril, Por copa, Espumoso, ¡Salud!). Send a note to the designer and Content that Spirits/Agave should sit above or beside Cocktails as the cantina's signature list, not at the bottom of the left column.

top_problem: Seven of the 11 non-cocktail descriptions add nothing a guest can use. Three (Blanco Tequila 'Blanco tequila pour.', Añejo Tequila 'Añejo tequila pour.', Cognac VSOP 'VSOP Cognac pour.') only repeat the item name, which is the criterion-12 automatic fail. Four more are catalogue labels: Malbec 'Dry red wine.', Pinot Grigio 'Dry white wine.', Dry Cider 'Dry sparkling cider.', Brut Rosé 'Dry sparkling rosé.'. The four cocktail lines read like a spec sheet ('Shaken, served on the rocks.') rather than guest language. Each cocktail fact does trace to a row: phg.menu_items for draft ddc4bb5b plus the phg.recipe_versions it links to. Margarita: garnish 'Lime wheel', glass 'Rocks', 'Shake with ice and strain over fresh ice'. Manhattan: 'Cocktail cherry', 'Coupe', 'Stir with ice and strain'. Brown Butter Old Fashioned: 'Orange peel', 'Rocks', 'strain over a large cube'. House Daiquiri: 'Lime coin', 'Coupe', 'fine strain'. One accuracy break: the Manhattan's draft menu_description is 'Rye, sweet vermouth, aromatic bitters.', but the print drops the bitters, so the printed drink is not the venue's spec. Unit prices all match menu_items (15/15/16/14/7/8/7/8/12/11/13/12/16/18). The retired Junmai Ginjo ($12) is correctly left off and flagged in proposal.md. On layout: name and price share a baseline (0.0 pt delta) and descriptions sit tight under names. But no price has a serve label: no oz on the wine, spirit or beer pours, and nothing tells the guest whether Brut Rosé is a glass or a bottle. The right column also runs one-line thin descriptions over large empty gaps under Beer, Cider and Wine while the left column is full.
fixes: Replace the three name-echo spirit lines and the four catalogue-label wine and cider lines with guest-facing copy built only from sourced facts. If no producer, region or tasting fact exists yet, keep a short flagged placeholder in doc.meta instead of printing a repeat of the name (this alone lifts criterion 12 above the automatic fail).

Restore 'aromatic bitters' to the Manhattan (source: phg.menu_items.menu_description 'Rye, sweet vermouth, aromatic bitters.'), e.g. 'Rye whiskey, sweet vermouth, aromatic bitters; cocktail cherry.' without adding a third line.

Rewrite the cocktail tails from spec-sheet voice into guest voice that keeps the sourced serve (rocks, coupe, large cube), and fix the awkward 'lime / wheel' break in the Margarita by rebalancing the wording.

Add pour and serve labels next to prices once sizes are supplied (oz for wine by the glass, spirit pours and draft beer; say whether Brut Rosé is a glass or a bottle). Until then, a 'glass' kicker on the Wine subheader is the minimum so the $11-13 figures are not unlabelled (layout note for the designer).

Venue fit: the agave list in a cantina is two generic pours with no brand and no mezcal. Ask for brand and agave data (public.brands / spirit_lexicon) and lead Spirits with agave in more depth. Also ask the designer to use the space left empty in the right column rather than letting Beer, Cider and Wine float (layout note).
